en.title: Street Fighter Eyes Box Office Crown Over Holmes Doc and Whale Thriller
en.summary: This weekend's box office is a fascinating clash of genres, with the iconic 'Street Fighter' video game franchise making a strong bid for the top spot. It faces stiff competition from a buzzy documentary about Elizabeth Holmes and a tense survival thriller.
en.body:
Get ready for a cinematic showdown this weekend as **Paramount's** highly anticipated **‘Street Fighter’** adaptation is projected to dominate the North American box office. Industry insiders are forecasting an impressive opening weekend haul of $25 million to $35 million, drawing in an estimated 3,500 theaters. This marks a significant opening for the latest attempt to translate the beloved fighting game franchise to the big screen, a feat that has historically proven challenging.

Meanwhile, the documentary circuit is abuzz with **A24's** **‘You Can See Everything’**, a deep dive into the controversial life of **Elizabeth Holmes**. This buzzy film, featuring **Nathan Fielder** and **Lance Oppenheim**, is expected to make a significant splash, aiming for $7 million to $8 million from a more limited release of just 800 locations. The film's presales at Alamo Drafthouse have already set a record for A24, even surpassing the second-highest presales for **‘Avengers: Doomsday’**, signaling strong audience interest.

## A Tale of Three Films

Adding to the diverse cinematic landscape is **Disney's** survival thriller **‘Whalefall’**. This tense tale is predicted to secure a strong second place at the box office, with estimates ranging from $10 million to $12 million from 3,065 venues. The weekend also sees the arrival of **Focus Features'** remake of **Jane Austen's** classic, though specific box office projections for this period drama have not been widely detailed.

This eclectic mix of genres – action, documentary, and survival thriller – highlights the varied appetites of moviegoers. **‘Street Fighter’** taps into the nostalgia and broad appeal of a globally recognized brand, while **‘You Can See Everything’** capitalizes on the public's fascination with true crime and cautionary tales of Silicon Valley ambition. **‘Whalefall’** offers pure, unadulterated suspense, promising a thrilling cinematic experience.

## What's Next for Audiences

The success of **‘Street Fighter’** will be a key indicator for the viability of video game adaptations, a genre that has seen mixed results over the years. The strong performance of **‘You Can See Everything’** underscores the continued audience demand for compelling documentary narratives, especially those exploring complex, real-world figures. As these films battle for box office supremacy, audiences have a rich and varied selection to choose from, ensuring a dynamic weekend at the movies.
